Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

business noun

what concerns someone

also none of your business, mind your own business, it’s none of my business, that’s my business, what’s that to you?, what’s it to me?, it’s my business to, it’s my job to, I mind my own business, mind one’s own business

classical

Ter. Haut. 75–76
Plaut. Trin. 4.2.136: quid id ad mē attinet? (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 94: nihil ad mē attinet
Plaut. Poen. 3.3.24: Quid istuc ad mē attinet? (Lewis & Short s.v. attineō)
Traupman 111: quid ad tē attinet?
Traupman 285: quid id ad tē attinet?

nihil ad tē attinet

phrase: attineō with ad

it’s none of your business

Attinet ad mē, it concerns me, is the usual classical sense of the verb (Lewis & Short). What business is it of yours? Quid id ad tē attinet? (Traupman 94).

Other words

  • ipse vīderit — that’s his business: let him see to it

    phrase: perfect subjunctive of videō · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.21.1; M-O s.v. business: that’s his business

  • aliēna negōtia cūrāre — to mind other people’s business

    phrase · also used · modern · Traupman 104

    After Terence’s aliēna ut cūrēs. Minding one’s own is sua negōtia cūrāre (Traupman 104); I always mind my own business, meum negōtium agō semper (Traupman 94).

  • suum negōtium agere — mind one’s own business

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.9 (Lewis & Short s.v. agō); Traupman 285

  • negōtium suum agere — mind one’s own business

    also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.9.29: suum negōtium agere (Lewis & Short s.v. negōtium); Traupman 345

Examples

  • tantumne est ab rē tuā ōtī tibi, aliēna ut cūrēs, eaque nihil quae ad tē attinent?

    have you so much time to spare from your own affairs that you mind other people’s, things that are none of your business?Ter. Haut. 75–76

  • sed ipse vīderit

    but that’s his businessCic. Att. 12.21.1

  • Meum est vidēre quid agātur.

    It’s my business to see what’s going on.Traupman 94

  • Negōtium agō semper meum.

    I always mind my own business.Traupman 285

See also business, interest, concern.
